quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the engine.
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: When power steering fails, you need to push harder on the steering wheel to control the car. Slow down and pull off the road to stop in a safe place.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the hardest season to drive in.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid often in winter.
Cruise control is safe to use in winter weather.
Snow tires are the best choice for winter driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cruise control is safe to use in winter weather.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or similar bad conditions. Winter is the hardest driving season and needs extra care. Check antifreeze and windshield washer fluid regularly. Snow tires help your car grip slippery roads better.

questions.question: Oregon's Implied Consent Law means that by driving in Oregon, you agree to:

options.text: Keep liability insurance as long as you drive.
Take a breath, blood, or urine test if arrested for drunk driving.
Post bail or go to court if arrested for a traffic violation.
Keep your vehicle's equipment in good working condition.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a breath, blood, or urine test if arrested for drunk driving.
questions.explanation: The Implied Consent Law means that by driving in Oregon, you agree to take a breath, blood, or urine test if a police officer asks you after arresting you for drunk driving.

questions.question: You should use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane because:

options.text: The person is a police officer.

questions.explanation: A white cane means the pedestrian is blind. Slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be ready to stop. Be careful to avoid hitting the pedestrian.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the road.
Speed up and steer back onto the road slowly.
Gently brake and turn the steering wheel to get back on the road at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently brake and turn the steering wheel to get back on the road at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: Keep your wheels off the pavement and slow down by gently pressing the brakes. When you are at a safe speed, turn the steering wheel to return to the road. Do not jerk the steering wheel sharply.

questions.question: What is the main danger shown by this sign?

options.text: Your headlights will point in different directions because one side of your car is higher.
You may damage a tire by drifting onto the shoulder.
You may hydroplane if there is water on the shoulder.
You may lose control of your vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may lose control of your vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: This sign means the shoulder is lower than the road. If one wheel drops onto the low shoulder, do not brake hard or steer sharply. This can cause you to lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Fines double in a work zone.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign warns drivers that bicycles may cross the road ahead.

questions.question: When you see a red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if there is no other traffic.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is watching.

questions.explanation: You must stop at a red light. It is illegal and dangerous to drive through a red light. You may turn right at a red light only if a sign does not say you cannot.

questions.question: When can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public highway?

options.text: As long as you are not the driver.
If you are in the back seat.
If you are in the back of a pickup truck.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have an open alcoholic container in any vehicle on a public road or sidewalk. This applies to all passengers, not just the driver.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, the driver should:

options.text: Drive normally because emotions do not affect driving.
Drive faster because they are more alert.
Calm down and focus on driving before starting the engine.
Call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus on driving before starting the engine.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions like worry, anger, and sadness take your attention away from driving. They can make it hard to drive safely. Calm yourself and get focused before you drive.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are crossing illegally.
Give pedestrians the right-of-way only when they have the legal right to cross.
Slow down and honk your horn near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are crossing illegally.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle. It is your job as a driver to watch for pedestrians and give them the right-of-way at all times, even if they are crossing where they should not.

questions.question: When there is an oncoming car to the left and a bicyclist to the right, you should:

options.text: Let the car pass and then pass the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass and then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: When you face more than one hazard, deal with one at a time. Do not try to squeeze between the oncoming car and the bicyclist at the same time. Instead, let the car pass first, then pass the bicyclist.

questions.question: A red traffic light means you must:
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop before entering the intersection. You must stop at the stop line and before entering the crosswalk.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down, stay alert, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Fog reduces how well you can see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road and objects better.

questions.explanation: Fog makes it hard to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, drive slowly and carefully. Do not use high beams. Low beams work better for seeing the road and objects ahead in fog.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means a ____ light will appear soon.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light is coming next.

questions.question: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn to warn drivers.
Stick part of your car onto the roadway to alert other drivers.
Drive out fast to blend in with traffic.
Give the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must give the right-of-way to all pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and dangers. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Adjust your speed to avoid brake damage or crashes.

questions.question: You notice a vehicle defect that could affect safe driving. You should:

options.text: Fix the defect when you have money.

questions.explanation: Any defect that affects safe driving must be fixed right away, before you drive the vehicle.

questions.question: A regulatory sign with a red circle and slash means:

options.text: Some drivers must yield to others.

questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that forbid actions are rectangular and white with red and black markings. A red circle with a slash through a symbol means that action is forbidden.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A series of curves is ahead.
The road will be slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will be slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road becomes very slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually ____ and you must always obey them.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs control traffic flow. They are white with black markings and drivers must always obey them.

questions.question: Highway signs that tell drivers about dangerous conditions are called:
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to possible hazards ahead. Follow warning signs to stay safe. Ignoring a warning sign can lead to accidents.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance between you and the car in front.
Drive in the right lane only.
Drive slower than the traffic around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance between you and the car in front.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance lets you react to problems ahead without sudden stops. Sudden stops can cause the car behind you to crash into you.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have bigger blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the back that drivers cannot see in their mirrors.

questions.question: Your car hits a parked car and you cannot find the owner. You must:

options.text: Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car, try to find the owner. If you cannot, leave a written note with your name, address, and details about the accident.

questions.question: When driving on ice or snow, which technique helps avoid crashes?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle for better grip.
Exit highways as quickly as possible.
Slow down and stay farther back from other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther back from other cars.
questions.explanation: Drive slower on snow and ice. Slower speed and more distance between cars are the best ways to avoid crashes in bad weather.

questions.question: Another driver is passing your car. You should:

options.text: Signal to tell them when it is safe to pass.
Check for oncoming cars and adjust your speed to help them pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming cars and adjust your speed to help them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay right when another driver passes you on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed so they can move back into the right lane easily.

questions.question: To reduce tiredness on a long drive, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Keep one eye open at a time.
Switch feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop for a break every two hours on long trips to avoid fatigue. If you feel drowsy, pull over safely and rest or find a place to sleep.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the center line means:
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: Lines that divide traffic moving in opposite directions are ____ colored.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: Which of these helps you avoid alcohol-related crashes?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Say no if someone offers you a drink while driving.

questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drinking and driving is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it harder to make safe choices after drinking starts.

questions.question: When can you cross a dashed white line?

options.text: When it is safe to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You can cross them to pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What do downward-facing triangular signs mean?
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs tell drivers to yield. When the road is clear and safe, you may proceed.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and return when safe.
Speed up and steer back onto the road quickly.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then ease back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then ease back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: If your right wheels leave the pavement, stay calm. Release the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and ease back onto the roadway. Keep both hands on the wheel and use a small steering movement. Check for traffic before returning to the road.
